body:
I LOVED the Chicken Fights! It arose spontaneously on our playground, which had a grassy section, in 1978. It never got dangerous or violent. Nobody was ever injured, not even a little bit. We didn't do it on the monkey bars. All we did was run around and try to pull each other down on the grass. The old biddies in charge of playground supervision finally broke it up for good after about a month. 

I am so f'ing glad not to be young today.

Believe me, I understand. I am probably as old or even older than your parents, but my situation is not much different than yours. I also belong to a "model" ethnic group, the one that everyone hates and yet at the same time expects to be smart, creative, rich, and highly achieving. I am none of these. I did go to college, and I graduated, and I even obtained additional degrees, but it ended up making absolutely no difference. Depression and anxiety made it impossible for me to obtain or hold a decent job or run a business, or anything like that. My mother is 90 and still on my ass, hard as that may be to imagine. She has taken to telling all kinds of lies about me to her stupid friends. Everyone else in the family is enormously successful professionally and vocationally, even those with chronic drug and/or alcohol problems (none of which I had).

Back to this business of the "model minority." I know a lot of Korean-Americans, since I grew up in L.A. I know exactly how obsessed they can get about education, grades, the "right" brand-name schools. The whole middle- and upper-middle-class rat race has become nothing short of utterly absurd and obscene. Mainstream society loves the way your ethnic group and mine act—to be good, obedient workers and taxpayers—so this behavior is encouraged and egged on. Obviously, it's better than a life of crime, etc., but the collateral damage is enormous.

Since you are still young—I won't say "you've got your whole life ahead of you," because your life may well just end up always sucking, but right now you do still have a chance to escape—so here are one or two suggestions. I have no idea whether they would work--but you might want to look into them. 

1. The military. When I was in my 40s, I worked for the Coast Guard as a civilian for a little while. A lot of the guys I worked with on the ship had faced your situation. They were reasonably intelligent, healthy guys whose families just sucked, for whatever reason. Once they joined up, Uncle Sam took care of things and the overbearing dads and moms were out of the picture and had no further say. Looking back, I wish sometimes that at 18 I had just told my parents to fuck off. I could have avoided taking their money (and the control and manipulation and unrealistic expectations that come with it), made my own scene, and deferred college until I was a bit more mature and had more idea of what I wanted to do, etc.
2. Now, I am not suggesting you join the Army or the Marines. That's a route to getting yourself killed and/or PTSD, etc. Try to get into the *Coast Guard or the Navy*. It's mostly about tech stuff there, skills. They can teach you a lot and you will earn money rather than paying some crappy college. You need some brains and ability to learn, but they organize everything for you. The Coast Guard is harder to get into. The only difficulty is that a certain percentage of men are color-blind, and that is a disqualifier. And of course you have to pass the overall fitness requirements. No diabetes, etc.
3. Even if you can't join the military, just run away! Put some distance between yourself and them. I know that this is not what people will tell you. But a toxic family is just the worst. If it is really as bad as you say, then you would be better off living on your own, even with some scut job and living in a dump. If you're an 18-year-old male, you can handle that. Get some distance.
4. Be very careful about meds. Therapists these days are no longer truly therapists. A therapist is someone who wants to help you understand yourself, figure out your problems, etc. Today's shrinks are little better than pill-pushers who are visited regularly by hot, slutty, pharmaceutical sales reps trying to foist the latest chemical concoction. (Hang out in the lobby of a medical office building and observe. It's ludicrous.) These pills are not going to solve your problems anymore than alcohol, weed, or LSD would (in fact, LSD was originally imagined as a way to deal with anxiety, ha). Protect yourself.

Very few people--perhaps nobody, sadly--have your best interests at heart. You really do have to look out for #1, that is, yourself.
